deep.reconstruction:
This page is fol. 4r (Riemann's own pagination '5') of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847, published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke, 1876). The page contains no computation. It states a requirement and announces a digression on series.

(a) The requirement on K_nu. The previous page defines the generalized 'Ableitung' d^nu z by the two-sided series
  (2) z(x+h) = sum_{nu = -inf}^{+inf} K_nu * d^nu z(x) * h^nu,
where the exponents nu differ from one another by integers. Here, (1) is the ordinary Taylor series
  (1) z(x+h) = sum_{n>=0} z^{(n)}(x) h^n / n!.
Riemann demands that K_nu be chosen so that (2) becomes (1) whenever the exponents are integers. Only then are the ordinary derivatives genuinely special cases of the 'Ableitungen'. Otherwise the definition would fail its purpose, which is to define an operation containing differentiation as a special case, and another route would have to be sought.

My own completion, which Riemann carries out on later pages and in the published text: comparing coefficients in (1) and (2) with d^n = d^n/dx^n gives K_n = 1/n! for n >= 0. The terms with negative integer n must drop out, or equivalently 1/K_n = 0 there. Both conditions are met by K_nu = 1/Gamma(nu+1), since 1/Gamma has zeros at the negative integers. In the published essay Riemann indeed arrives at K_nu = 1/Pi(nu) = 1/Gamma(nu+1).

(b) The digression on series. Before determining K_nu, Riemann wants to say something about series of this two-sided form, because they are the foundation of the whole theory. He reports a claimed view that no safe conclusions may be drawn from series unless their quantities take values making the series converge, i.e. unless the (at least approximate) value can be found by actual numerical addition. The next page rebuts this. A series whose coefficients obey a definite law is, in all its parts, a determinate quantity, so the rules of arithmetic may be applied to it even when term-by-term addition fails. This is an early-19th-century formalist stance on divergent series.
errors: No mathematical error on this page, since there is no derivation.

The formalist position Riemann adopts (via the next page), that divergent series with lawful coefficients may be manipulated freely, is not rigorous by modern standards. The ex-post-facto fix is analytic continuation or summability theory.

The implicit claim that the integer case fixes K_nu for all real nu is not justified at this point. The integer values do not determine K_nu uniquely; the extension to 1/Gamma(nu+1) needs further conditions, supplied later in the essay.

results.what: Normalization requirement: the generalized fractional derivative series (2) must reduce to Taylor's series for integer orders, which forces K_n = 1/n! (eventually K_nu = 1/Gamma(nu+1)).
results.modern_name: Taylor-Riemann series / generalized Taylor expansion underlying Riemann-Liouville fractional calculus
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1847 essay, publ. 1876); the series idea goes back to Liouville (1832) and to Lagrange's 'fonctions dérivées' for the terminology

results.what: Methodological remark that divergent series with lawful coefficients are determinate quantities to which the laws of arithmetic apply.
results.modern_name: Formal or divergent series (pre-Cauchy/Abel formalism; cf. Euler, Peacock's principle of permanence)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange; the formalist tradition criticized by Cauchy (1821) and Abel (1826)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of Riemann's well-known 1847 student essay on fractional differentiation, printed in his Werke since 1876. Its content is purely verbal: the Taylor-compatibility requirement and a preface to a discussion of divergent series. Nothing here is unknown or attributed to someone else.

checkable.asserts: K_nu = 1/Gamma(nu+1) agrees with the Taylor coefficients 1/n! for nonnegative integers n.
1/Gamma(nu+1) vanishes at negative integer nu, so the negative-index terms disappear in the integer case and (2) reduces to (1).

checkable.sympy: simplify(series((x+h)**mu, h, 0, 4).removeO() - sum(gamma(mu+1)/(gamma(mu-n+1)*gamma(n+1))*x**(mu-n)*h**n for n in range(4)))
checkable.asserts: For z = x**mu, the derivatives of the integer Taylor series (1) are Gamma(mu+1)/Gamma(mu-n+1) x**(mu-n), consistent with K_n = 1/Gamma(n+1). Result should be 0, possibly after expand/gammasimp.

transcription_corrections: 'Reihe [-K-]convergiren[?]' — the image shows the word beginning with a struck-through 'K'. The intended reading is 'convergire' (subjunctive, matching 'daß die Reihe convergire'), not 'convergiren'.

Otherwise the transcription agrees with the image: 'Differentialquotienten', 'Ableitungen', 'entsprechend', 'Versuchs einer Theorie der Ableitungen', 'Ziffern-[addition]'. The '5' at top right is Riemann's own page number; the pencil '4' in the margin is the folio number.
